    - text: PHASE 1 · STATISTICAL INFERENCE
    - heading "p-Values" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Read a p-value as surprise under a null model, not as the probability a claim is true.
    - text: "#2014 · 15 min · Advanced · Statistical Inference"
    - heading "Tail-Area Explorer" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Explore p-values using the standard normal null model (mean = 0, SD = 1).
    - heading "Alternative hypothesis (H₁)" [level=3]
    - group "Alternative hypothesis":
      - button "Left-tailed"
      - button "Right-tailed"
      - button "Two-sided" [pressed]
    - text: Observed z
    - spinbutton "Observed z numeric": "2"
    - slider "Observed z slider": "2"
    - paragraph: "-3.5 3.5"

    - heading "Two-sided p-value" [level=3]
    - strong: "0.0455"
    - text: (4.55%)
    - paragraph: Area in both tails beyond ±2.00
    - math: p = 2 P ( Z ≥ 2.00 )
    - paragraph: p ≈ 0.0455. Tail probabilities include the portions beyond the plotted axis.
    - button "Reset":
      - img
      - text: Reset
    - heading "Null Model Simulation (1,000 trials)" [level=2]
    - paragraph: One dot per generated standard-normal statistic under H₀. Dots are stacked in narrow z bins; tail counts use unrounded values.
    - text: Not as extreme (952) At least as extreme (48)
    - button "Generate a new null sample":
      - img
    - img "1000 simulated z statistics, 48 at least as extreme as observed": "-3 -2 -1 0 1 2 3"
    - heading "Simulated p-value (two-sided)" [level=3]
    - strong: "0.048"
    - paragraph: 48 out of 1,000 simulated statistics are at least as extreme. Seed 1. The estimate varies between runs; it is not the exact tail probability.
    - article:
      - heading "What Is a p-Value?" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A p-value describes how often the specified null model would produce a test statistic at least as extreme as observed, in the direction specified by the alternative.
      - text: Assume H₀
      - img
      - text: Null distribution
      - img
      - text: At least as extreme
      - img
      - text: Tail probability
      - button "Learn more about p-values":
        - img
        - text: Learn more about p-values
    - article:
      - heading "Compare With α = 0.05" [level=2]
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "p-value Comparison with α = 0.05":
            - columnheader "p-value"
            - columnheader "Comparison with α = 0.05"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "0.0455 p < α Statistically significant at 5%.":
            - cell "0.0455"
            - cell "p < α Statistically significant at 5%."
          - row "p ≥ 0.05 Fail to reject H₀ under the decision rule.":
            - cell "p ≥ 0.05"
            - cell "Fail to reject H₀ under the decision rule."
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: A threshold comparison is not a measure of effect size or the probability that a hypothesis is true.
    - heading "Common Misconceptions" [level=2]
    - article:
      - heading "p is NOT P(H₀ is true)." [level=3]:
        - img
        - text: p is NOT P(H₀ is true).
      - paragraph: The p-value is calculated assuming H₀. It does not assign H₀ a probability.
    - article:
      - heading "p is NOT an effect size." [level=3]:
        - img
        - text: p is NOT an effect size.
      - paragraph: A smaller p-value does not tell you how large or important an effect is.
    - article:
      - heading "p is NOT the probability the results occurred by chance." [level=3]:
        - img
        - text: p is NOT the probability the results occurred by chance.
      - paragraph: It concerns data at least as extreme under the specified null model, not the cause of the observed results.
    - 'heading "Practice: Interpret a p-Value" [level=2]'
    - paragraph: Read the scenario and interpret the reported p-value.
    - article:
      - heading "Scenario" [level=3]
      - paragraph: A new teaching method is tested for improved scores. Sample means are 78.2 for the new method and 73.4 for the traditional method. The reported one-sided two-sample t-test p-value is 0.03, for improvement.
    - article:
      - heading "Question" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Interpret this p-value under the test's null model and assumptions.
    - group "Interpretation choices":
      - text: Interpretation choices
      - radio "A. Assuming no improvement and the stated test assumptions, results at least as extreme in the improvement direction have probability 3% under the null model."
      - text: A. Assuming no improvement and the stated test assumptions, results at least as extreme in the improvement direction have probability 3% under the null model.
      - radio "B. There is a 3% probability the new method truly improves scores."
      - text: B. There is a 3% probability the new method truly improves scores.
      - radio "C. There is a 3% chance the observed results occurred by chance."
      - text: C. There is a 3% chance the observed results occurred by chance.
      - radio "D. The new method improves scores by 3%."
      - text: D. The new method improves scores by 3%.
